name: MAAT - Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
seoTitle: MAAT Lisbon: Riverside Roof Walk and Museum Tickets
tagline: Walk over the roof for free; the galleries (€16) suit a longer call. Open Mondays, closed Tuesdays

description.short: MAAT is Lisbon's contemporary museum of art, architecture and technology, in a riverside gallery building by Amanda Levete's studio AL_A and the former Central Tejo power station. Opened in 2016 at the eastern end of Belém.
description.full:
MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology) sits on the riverfront at the eastern end of Belém, closer to the city than the other Belém sights. Unlike the Jerónimos Monastery and the Torre de Belém it is open on Mondays, but it is closed on Tuesdays; hours are 10:00 to 19:00, Wednesday to Monday. Belém railway station is about 7 minutes' walk away, which makes the Cascais-line train from Cais do Sodré an easy way in.

The campus has two parts. The low, curved gallery building by Amanda Levete's studio AL_A, clad in white three-dimensional ceramic tiles, has a roof designed as a public walkway you can climb and cross, with views of the 25 de Abril Bridge and the river. Next door, the brick Central Tejo power station houses MAAT Central, where the old plant's machinery sits alongside the galleries. Exhibitions change: in autumn 2026 the programme includes a large Pedro Cabrita Reis show and 'Turn around', about 90 works from the EDP Foundation Art Collection at MAAT Central until January 2027.

For a cruise passenger, the question is whether to pay. The €16 ticket for non-residents suits contemporary art and architecture fans with at least an hour and a half to spare. On a short call, the roof and the riverside garden take 20–30 minutes and still show off the building. MAAT works as an afternoon add-on after Jerónimos, or as the Monday alternative when the national monuments are shut.

Distances are longer than they look on a map: the Padrão dos Descobrimentos is about 16 minutes' walk west along the river, Pastéis de Belém about 14 minutes and the Torre de Belém about 26 minutes. MAAT Café & Kitchen in the gallery building serves food with river views. Admission is free on 4 and 5 October 2026 for the museum's 10th anniversary.
description.history: The Central Tejo power station was built from 1908 by the Companhias Reunidas de Gás e Electricidade and supplied electricity to Lisbon for decades before being decommissioned. Listed as a building of public interest in 1986, it opened as the Electricity Museum in 1990. In October 2016 the EDP Foundation relaunched the site as MAAT, adding the new riverside gallery designed by AL_A and a landscaped garden by Vladimir Djurovic linking the two buildings. The contrast between the brick-and-iron power plant and the white, low-slung gallery is the point of the visit.
description.significance: MAAT is one of Lisbon's main venues for contemporary art, architecture and technology, run by the EDP Foundation. It pairs one of the city's best-known pieces of 21st-century architecture with a surviving early-20th-century industrial building, so it shows a side of Belém that has nothing to do with the Discoveries. Its roof and garden also work as a public riverside space used by locals, not only museum visitors.

directions.general: Located on the Tagus River waterfront in Belém district, between Jerónimos Monastery and 25 de Abril Bridge
directions.fromCruisePort: About 6.4 km west on the Belém riverfront, not walkable on a port day. Taxi about 15 minutes; or the Cascais-line train from Cais do Sodré to Belém and a 10-minute walk east along the river. The Jerónimos Monastery is about 1 km further west.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to Altinho stop (5-minute walk from museum). Trains from Cais do Sodré to Belém station (10-minute walk). Buses 728, 714, 727, 729, 751. Free shuttle from Cais do Sodré weekends.
directions.parking: Free public parking 500m from museum. Bicycle parking available at entrance.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open Wednesday to Monday; closed on Tuesdays

admissionPrices.notes: Non-residents of Portugal: adults €16, students under 30 with card €12 (25% off), seniors 65+ 15% off (€13.60). Residents in Portugal: adults €12, students €9, seniors 65+/unemployed €10.20. Children 0–12 free. Free first Sunday of each month 10:00–13:00 (residents in Portugal only). Free on 4 and 5 October 2026 (10th anniversary). Discounts cannot be combined; ID required.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 20–30 minutes for the roof and garden; 1.5–2 hours with the exhibitions
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Weekday mornings less crowded. Late afternoon for beautiful light on the building and river views. Sunset from the rooftop walkway is spectacular.
busyPeriods: First Sunday of the month (free for residents, 10:00-13:00)
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Walk over the gallery roof for river views. Visit both the gallery building and MAAT Central in the former power station. Large bags, umbrellas and pets are not allowed; lockers are available. The Padrão dos Descobrimentos is about 16 minutes' walk west along the river.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2 hours return from the ship for the roof and garden only; 3–3.5 hours with the exhibitions
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Good: lifts and ramps to the upper floors, adapted toilets and wheelchairs on loan. Belém station is about 7 minutes' walk.
tips: Closed on Tuesdays but open on Mondays, when the Jerónimos Monastery and the Torre de Belém are closed.
Take the Cascais-line train from Cais do Sodré to Belém: the station is about 7 minutes' walk from the museum.
Short on time? The roof walkway and riverside garden take 20–30 minutes and are public spaces.
Non-resident tickets: €16 adult, €12 with a student card (under 30); seniors 65+ get 15% off; under-12s free. Discounts cannot be combined.
Free admission on 4 and 5 October 2026 for MAAT's 10th anniversary; expect it to be busier than usual.
Large bags, umbrellas and pets are not allowed inside; lockers are available.
Lifts and ramps reach the upper floors, and two wheelchairs can be borrowed at the ticket offices.
Allow for the walk: 16 minutes to the Padrão dos Descobrimentos and 26 minutes to the Torre de Belém.

highlights: Walkable roof of the AL_A gallery building, with views of the river and the 25 de Abril Bridge
Façade of white three-dimensional ceramic tiles
MAAT Central: galleries inside the brick Central Tejo power station, with its original machinery
'Turn around': about 90 works from the EDP Foundation Art Collection (until January 2027)
Pedro Cabrita Reis exhibition 'without sorrow of heart' (autumn 2026)
Riverside MAAT Garden linking the two buildings
MAAT Café & Kitchen and a shop focused on Portuguese design

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Lift and ramp access to the upper floors, adapted toilets, and two wheelchairs available on request at the ticket offices.
